tools.description: Get details of the teams the user is a member of. Limited to organizations accessible with current credentials. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's get_teams: a bare array of {org, teams: [{name, slug, description}]} for every organization this universe records (a repository owner with no personal account row, or an organization account, plus any organization a teams or issue_types row names); teams come from the loaded team rosters, so an organization with none recorded answers teams []; user omitted means the caller github_get_me reports, and a login with no account row answers Not Found.

user.description: Username to get teams for. If not provided, uses the authenticated user. Null and "" mean the authenticated user (the login github_get_me reports); a login with no account row answers Not Found.
user.title: User

tools.name: github_get_user
tools.description: Get a user by login.

username.description: GitHub user login (handle) to look up.
username.title: Username

tools.name: github_issue_read
tools.description: Get information about a specific issue in a GitHub repository. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's issue_read: method get answers the issue row, get_comments the conversation comments (bare array, paged by page/perPage), get_sub_issues the issues whose parent is this one (paged), get_parent the parent issue row and get_labels {labels, totalCount}; a method outside that vocabulary is refused with a validation error naming it, and an unknown issue answers Not Found.

method.description: Action to specify what issue data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. One of "get" (the issue row), "get_comments" (the conversation comments, oldest first, as a bare array paged by page/perPage), "get_sub_issues" (the issues whose parent is this one, by number, paged), "get_parent" (the parent issue row; Not Found when the issue has none) or "get_labels" ({labels, totalCount}). Any other value is refused with a validation error naming method.
method.title: Method

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

tools.name: github_issue_write
tools.description: Create a new or update an existing issue in a GitHub repository. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's issue_write: method create adds the issue (title required) as github_create_issue does, method update patches the issue issue_number names (required) as github_update_issue does, every other field omit-to-leave-unchanged; a method outside that vocabulary is refused with a validation error naming it.

method.description: Operation to perform: "create" (a new issue; title is required) or "update" (an existing issue; issue_number is required, every other field is omit-to-leave-unchanged). Any other value is refused with a validation error naming method.
method.title: Method

title.description: Issue title. Required for create; on update, omit to leave unchanged.
title.title: Title

body.description: Issue body (markdown). On create, omitted, "" and null all mean an empty body; on update, omit to leave unchanged.
body.title: Body

labels.description: Label names: attached to the new issue on create; the replacement set on update.
labels.title: Labels

assignees.description: User logins: assigned to the new issue on create; the replacement set on update.
assignees.title: Assignees

milestone.description: Milestone number to associate with the issue, stored as given and echoed as milestone {number, url, html_url}; on update, 0 removes the current milestone and omitting leaves it unchanged.
milestone.title: Milestone

state_reason.description: Update only. Reason for the state change, ignored unless state is changed. One of "completed", "not_planned" or "duplicate"; closing without one records completed and reopening records reopened. Any other value is refused.
state_reason.title: State Reason

duplicate_of.description: Update only. Issue number that this issue is a duplicate of. Required when state_reason is 'duplicate' and refused otherwise; it must name an issue or pull request of the same repository.
duplicate_of.title: Duplicate Of

issue_number.description: Issue number to update. Required for update, ignored on create.
issue_number.title: Issue Number

tools.name: github_label_write
tools.description: Perform write operations on repository labels. To set labels on issues, use the 'update_issue' tool. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's label_write: method create adds the label (color is required for create), update patches it (at least one of new_name, color, or description must be provided for update) and delete removes it, as github_create_label, github_update_label and github_delete_label do; a method outside that vocabulary is refused with a validation error naming it.

method.description: Operation to perform: "create" (color is required), "update" (at least one of new_name, color or description) or "delete". Any other value is refused with a validation error naming method.
method.title: Method

name.description: Label name: the name of the new label on create, the current name on update and delete.
name.title: Name

new_name.description: New label name, update only. Omit to leave unchanged; a rename also rewrites the label on every issue and pull request that carries it.
new_name.title: New Name

color.description: 6-character hex color (without the leading #). Required for create, optional for update; stored verbatim.
color.title: Color

description.description: Short description shown on label hover. Optional for create and update.
description.title: Description

tools.name: github_list_branches
tools.description: List branches. Mirrors GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/branches; every row carries commit ({sha, url}, or null when no head is known).

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

tools.name: github_list_commit_statuses
tools.description: List the commit statuses of a reference, newest first. Mirrors GET /repos/{o}/{r}/commits/{ref}/statuses: every status ever posted for the commit (the history, several per context), each {id, url, state, description, target_url, context, created_at, updated_at, creator}, as a bare array paged by page and perPage (30 by default, up to 100), plus one mirrored status per simulated CI check run on that commit (pending while it runs, its conclusion once complete). An unknown repository or ref answers Not Found; an unknown hex sha No commit found for SHA.

ref.description: Commit SHA (full, or a unique prefix of at least 7 hex characters), branch name (also heads/BRANCH_NAME) or tag name (tags/TAG_NAME) whose statuses are read. A branch or tag resolves to its recorded head; an unknown hex sha answers No commit found for SHA (status 422), any other unknown ref Not Found.
ref.title: Ref

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

tools.name: github_list_commits
tools.description: List commits, newest first. Mirrors GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/commits: every commit the repository clone reaches from the ref (the commit store is completed from the clone when the universe loads); `path` narrows to the commits touching that file, `fields` names the row keys to return, and page with `page` while `has_more` is true.

sha.description: SHA, branch or tag to start listing commits from (defaults to the repository's default branch; `HEAD` names it too). The listing covers every commit the repository clone reaches from that ref: the commit store is completed from the clone when the universe loads. A ref that names no branch, tag or commit answers the Not Found error envelope.
sha.title: Sha

path.description: Only commits containing this file path will be returned. A repository with no git history, or a `sha` the clone cannot resolve, cannot answer it — there the filter is skipped and the envelope says so in `unpopulated_fields`. A path escaping the repository or reading as an option is refused by name.
path.title: Path

author.description: Filter by the commit author's GitHub login or email address (both case-insensitive); an empty value applies no filter.
author.title: Author

since.description: Only commits after this date are returned, compared against the stored authored date. Two forms: an RFC 3339 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, an offset such as +02:00 in place of Z, an optional fraction of a second, accepted and compared at whole-second granularity) or a date YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC). Any other value is refused naming the parameter.
since.title: Since

until.description: Only commits before this date are returned, compared against the stored authored date. Two forms: an RFC 3339 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, an offset such as +02:00 in place of Z, an optional fraction of a second, accepted and compared at whole-second granularity) or a date YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC). Any other value is refused naming the parameter.
until.title: Until

perPage.description: Page size: 1-30, default 30; up to 100 when `fields` narrows the rows. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped and the envelope's perPage echoes the size applied.
perPage.title: Perpage

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each commit. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields, e.g. just 'sha' and 'html_url'. Names: sha, html_url, commit, author, committer, parents. sha is always included; up to 100 rows are served when fields is given; an empty or unknown name is refused.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: github_list_issue_fields
tools.description: List issue fields for a repository or organization. Returns field definitions including name, type (text, number, date, single_select), and for single_select fields the list of valid option names. When repo is omitted, returns org-level fields directly. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's list_issue_fields; this universe records no custom issue fields, so a known owner answers []; an owner that owns no repository, has no account row and is named by no team or issue type, or a repo this universe does not record, answers Not Found.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository or organization. The name is not case sensitive. An owner that owns no repository, has no account row and is named by no team or issue type answers Not Found.
owner.title: Owner

repo.description: The name of the repository. When provided, returns fields for this specific repository (inherited from its organization). When omitted, returns org-level fields directly. Null and "" mean omitted; a repository this universe does not record answers Not Found.
repo.title: Repo

tools.name: github_list_issue_types
tools.description: List supported issue types for a repository or its owner organization. When repo is omitted, returns org-level issue types directly. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's list_issue_types over the loaded issue_types collection: a bare array of {id, node_id, name, description, color, created_at, updated_at, is_enabled} rows of the owner (with repo, of that repository's owner), [] when the universe records none; an owner that owns no repository, has no account row and is named by no team or issue type, or a repo this universe does not record, answers Not Found.

owner.description: The account owner of the repository or organization. The name is not case sensitive. An owner that owns no repository, has no account row and is named by no team or issue type answers Not Found.
owner.title: Owner

repo.description: The name of the repository. When provided, returns issue types for this specific repository. When omitted, returns org-level issue types directly. Null and "" mean omitted; a repository this universe does not record answers Not Found.
repo.title: Repo

tools.name: github_list_issues
tools.description: List issues. Mirrors GET /repos/{o}/{r}/issues over the issues collection only (seeded empty for hg4 universes; github_create_issue populates them at runtime). Filters: state, labels (all of them), assignee, creator, milestone and since; order with sort (or the official orderBy) and direction — the default is created, newest first, with number descending as the tie-break. A value outside a declared vocabulary is refused with a validation error naming the parameter; `fields` names the row keys to return; page with `page` while `has_more` is true.

state.description: "open" | "closed" | "all" (the REST spellings) or "OPEN" | "CLOSED" (the official MCP spellings, folded). Default "open"; null and "" mean the default. Any other value is refused.
state.title: State

labels.description: Filter by label names: only issues carrying ALL of them are returned. An array of names, or one string of comma-separated names ("bug,ui", the REST spelling); omitted, null, [] and "" apply no filter.
labels.title: Labels

assignee.description: Filter by assignee login (case-insensitive). "none" selects issues with no assignee and "*" issues with any assignee. Omitted, null and "" apply no filter.
assignee.title: Assignee

creator.description: Filter by the login of the user that created the issue (case-insensitive). Omitted, null and "" apply no filter.
creator.title: Creator

milestone.description: Filter by milestone: a milestone number (an integer, or that integer as a string), "*" for issues with any milestone, "none" for issues without one. Omitted, null and "" apply no filter; any other value is refused.
milestone.title: Milestone

since.description: Only issues updated at or after this instant are returned, compared against the stored updated_at. Two forms: an RFC 3339 timestamp (YYYY-MM-DDThh:mm:ssZ, an offset such as +02:00 in place of Z, an optional fraction of a second) or a date YYYY-MM-DD (midnight UTC). Any other value is refused naming the parameter; null and "" mean omitted.
since.title: Since

sort.description: "created" | "updated" | "comments" (the REST spellings; comments is the number of conversation comments). Default "created"; null and "" mean the default. orderBy is the official MCP spelling of the same choice; when both are given they must agree. Any other value is refused.
sort.title: Sort

orderBy.description: "CREATED_AT" | "UPDATED_AT" | "COMMENTS" (the official MCP spellings of sort). Omitted, null and "" defer to sort. Any other value is refused.
orderBy.title: Orderby

direction.description: "asc" | "desc", also accepted as "ASC" | "DESC". Default "desc"; null and "" mean the default. Any other value is refused.
direction.title: Direction

perPage.description: Page size: 1-30, default 30; up to 100 when `fields` narrows the rows. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped and the envelope's perPage echoes the size applied.
perPage.title: Perpage

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each issue. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' and 'field_values' in particular drops the largest per-result data. Names: number, title, body, state, state_reason, user, labels, assignees, milestone, comments, reactions, duplicate_of, parent_issue_number, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, html_url, url, pull_request, field_values, id. number is always included; up to 100 rows are served when fields is given; an empty or unknown name is refused.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: github_list_labels
tools.description: List labels for a repository as a JSON array of {id, name, color, description} rows. Mirrors GET /repos/{o}/{r}/labels.

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

tools.name: github_list_pull_requests
tools.description: List pull requests. Mirrors GET /repos/{owner}/{repo}/pulls: sorted by created (newest first) unless sort says otherwise, direction defaulting to desc for created and asc for updated and popularity, as on GitHub; popularity is the number of conversation comments. A state, sort or direction outside its declared vocabulary is refused with a validation error naming the parameter in `invalid_fields`; `fields` names the row keys to return; page with `page` while `has_more` is true.

state.description: "open" | "closed" | "all". Default "open"; null and "" mean the default. Any other value is refused.
state.title: State

head.description: Filter by head branch, as `user:ref-name` / `organization:ref-name` or as a bare ref name. A prefix that is not this repository's owner names a fork and matches nothing.
head.title: Head

sort.description: "created" | "updated" | "popularity" (popularity orders by the number of conversation comments). Null means the default "created". Any other value is refused.
sort.title: Sort

direction.description: "asc" | "desc". Default: "desc" when sort is "created" or omitted, otherwise "asc", as on GitHub; null means the default. Any other value is refused.
direction.title: Direction

perPage.description: Page size: 1-30, default 30; up to 100 when `fields` narrows the rows. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped and the envelope's perPage echoes the size applied.
perPage.title: Perpage

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each pull request. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' in particular drops the largest per-result data. Names: the keys of a pull request row (number, title, body, state, draft, merged, mergeable, mergeable_state, html_url, url, user, labels, assignees, requested_reviewers, requested_teams, merged_by, head, base, merge_commit_sha, additions, deletions, changed_files, commits, comments, created_at, updated_at, closed_at, merged_at, milestone, locked, id, maintainer_can_modify, reactions). number is always included; up to 100 rows are served when fields is given; an empty or unknown name is refused.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: github_list_releases
tools.description: List releases. Mirrors GET /repos/{o}/{r}/releases; `fields` names the row keys to return; `resource_populated` is false when no release exists anywhere in this universe.

perPage.description: Page size: 1-30, default 30; up to 100 when `fields` narrows the rows. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped and the envelope's perPage echoes the size applied.
perPage.title: Perpage

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each release. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'body' in particular drops the largest per-release data. Names: id, tag_name, name, body, html_url, published_at, prerelease, draft, author, created_at, target_commitish. id and tag_name are always included; up to 100 rows are served when fields is given; an empty or unknown name is refused.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: github_list_repository_collaborators
tools.description: List collaborators for a repository as a JSON array of user rows ordered by login, each with permissions{pull, triage, push, maintain, admin} and role_name. The roster is the accounts recorded as authoring, committing to, reviewing, commenting on or being assigned in that repository's pull requests, issues and commits, plus the caller github_get_me reports; organization accounts are never listed. Mirrors GET /repos/{o}/{r}/collaborators.

affiliation.description: Filter by affiliation. Can be one of: 'outside' (outside collaborators), 'direct' (all with permissions regardless of org membership), 'all' (all collaborators). Default: 'all'. This universe records no outside collaborators, so "outside" answers an empty array; null and "" mean the default; any other value is refused.
affiliation.title: Affiliation

permission.description: Filter collaborators by the permissions they have on the repository. If not specified, all collaborators will be returned. Can be one of: pull, triage, push, maintain, admin. Every collaborator here holds the write role, so pull, triage and push return the whole roster and maintain and admin answer an empty array; null and "" mean not specified; any other value is refused.
permission.title: Permission

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

tools.name: github_list_tags
tools.description: List tags for a repository. Mirrors GET /repos/{o}/{r}/tags; `resource_populated` is false when no tag exists anywhere in this universe.

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100 and the envelope's perPage echoes the size applied.
perPage.title: Perpage

tools.name: github_merge_pull_request
tools.description: Merge a pull request and return {merged, sha, message}: merge writes a two-parent merge commit, squash one single-parent commit, rebase replays the head commits onto the base one by one (no merge commit; sha is the last replayed commit) — real commits in the repository clone where both refs resolve there (a conflicted path takes the head side), recorded in the store only elsewhere; the base branch head moves (and the working tree follows a merge into the checked-out default branch), the PR closes and a "merged" timeline event is inserted. An unknown number answers `Not Found`; a merge_method outside merge/squash/rebase is refused with a validation error naming it, merging nothing; expectedHeadSha (or its REST alias sha) that differs from the recorded head is refused with 409 Head branch was modified. Review and try the merge again.; an already-merged or otherwise unmergeable PR answers an error naming the reason.

pullNumber.description: Pull request number within the repository.
pullNumber.title: Pullnumber

merge_method.description: Merge strategy: "merge" (a two-parent merge commit), "squash" (one commit titled "<title> (#N)") or "rebase" (the head commits replayed one by one onto the base, no merge commit; commit_title and commit_message are ignored). Where both refs resolve in the repository clone the commit is written there and the base ref advances; elsewhere it is recorded in the store only. Null means "merge". Any other value is refused.
merge_method.title: Merge Method

commit_title.description: Title for the merge commit. Defaults to a GitHub-style auto-generated title.
commit_title.title: Commit Title

commit_message.description: Extra detail appended to the merge commit message.
commit_message.title: Commit Message

expectedHeadSha.description: The expected SHA of the pull request's HEAD ref. When given and the recorded head differs, the merge is refused with 409 Head branch was modified. Review and try the merge again.; a pull request whose head sha is not recorded cannot be checked and merges. Null and "" mean not given.
expectedHeadSha.title: Expectedheadsha

sha.description: REST spelling of expectedHeadSha: SHA that pull request head must match to allow merge. When both are given they must agree.
sha.title: Sha

tools.name: github_pull_request_read
tools.description: Get information on a specific pull request in GitHub repository. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's pull_request_read: method get answers the pull request row, get_diff {diff, truncated}, get_status the combined status, get_files the changed files with patch, get_commits the recorded pull-request commits (paged), get_review_comments the inline comments as review threads {review_threads, totalCount, pageInfo} (perPage and the after cursor), get_reviews the reviews, get_comments the conversation comments (bare array, paged) and get_check_runs the check runs of the live head ({total_count, check_runs}, paged); a method outside that vocabulary is refused with a validation error naming it, and an unknown pull request answers Not Found.

method.description: Action to specify what pull request data needs to be retrieved from GitHub. One of "get" (the pull request row), "get_diff" (the unified diff of base...head as text, whole, as the official server returns it; past 300 files, 800 lines or 40KB a 406 too_large refusal like GitHub gives), "get_status" (the combined commit status), "get_files" (the changed files with patch, paged), "get_commits" (the recorded pull-request commits, oldest first, paged), "get_review_comments" (the inline review comments grouped into threads, paged by perPage and the after cursor), "get_reviews" (the review objects), "get_comments" (the conversation comments, not the inline ones, as a bare array paged) or "get_check_runs" ({total_count, check_runs} for the live head, as github_get_check_runs answers with filter latest, paged by page/perPage). Any other value is refused with a validation error naming method.
method.title: Method

pullNumber.description: Pull request number within the repository.
pullNumber.title: Pullnumber

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

after.description: Cursor for pagination, used only by the get_review_comments method: the endCursor of a previous page (a non-negative integer counting threads). Omitted, null and "" start at the first thread; a value that is not such an integer is refused with a validation error naming after. Ignored by every other method.
after.title: After

tools.name: github_pull_request_review_write
tools.description: Create and/or submit, delete review of a pull request. Mirrors the official GitHub MCP server's pull_request_review_write: method create adds a review as github_create_pull_request_review does (with event submitted at once, without event a pending review, commitID the sha to review), submit_pending submits the caller's pending review with the given event (required) and body, delete_pending deletes it (answering {deleted, review}); with no pending review the answer is No pending review found for the viewer or The latest review, found at {url} is not pending. A method outside the vocabulary (including resolve_thread and unresolve_thread, not recorded here) is refused with a validation error naming it.

method.description: Operation to perform: "create" (a new review of the pull request: with event it is submitted at once, without event a pending review is created), "submit_pending" (submit the caller's pending review; event required, body optional) or "delete_pending" (delete the caller's pending review). Any other value, including the official resolve_thread and unresolve_thread, is refused with a validation error naming method.
method.title: Method

pullNumber.description: Pull request number within the repository.
pullNumber.title: Pullnumber

body.description: Review body text shown on the PR conversation. Omitted, null and "" mean an empty body on create; on submit_pending they keep the pending review's text.
body.title: Body

event.description: APPROVE | REQUEST_CHANGES | COMMENT. Omitted, null and "" leave a create pending (state PENDING, submitted later with submit_pending) and are refused on submit_pending; a value outside the vocabulary is refused.
event.title: Event

commitID.description: SHA of commit to review. Omitted, null and "" mean the pull request head sha; stored verbatim as commit_id on the review and its comments.
commitID.title: Commitid

tools.name: github_push_files
tools.description: Push multiple files in one commit and return {commit: {sha, message, author, url, html_url}, files: [{path, sha}, ...], ref, url, object: {type, sha, url}}. Writes the default branch through the working tree and any other branch through that branch's tree in the clone. Each entry's content is plain text, stored UTF-8 encoded. One bad entry (a non-string content, a path outside the repo, a duplicate path, or a supplied sha that no longer matches) refuses the whole push with an error naming the path. A branch that does not exist is created from the default branch head, as the official push_files does.

files.description: list of {"path": "...", "content": "<file content>", "sha": "<optional>"}. content is the file text verbatim — do not base64-encode it. sha is the path's current blob sha from github_get_file_contents — supply it to refuse the whole push if that path changed underneath you; omit it to overwrite.
files.title: Files

branch.description: The branch to push to; a branch that does not exist is created from the default branch head, as the official push_files does. Omitted and null mean the repository's default branch. Recorded on the commit and the branch head pointer; a write to a branch other than the default branch commits to that branch's own tree in the repository clone and leaves the default branch's files untouched, so an unqualified read (no ref) does not see it until it is merged.
branch.title: Branch

tools.name: github_remove_requested_reviewers
tools.description: Removes review requests from a pull request for a given set of users and/or teams. Mirrors DELETE /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers: each login or slug currently requested is removed and records a review_request_removed timeline event; one not requested is left alone without error. The answer is the updated pull request row; an unknown pull request answers Not Found.

pullNumber.description: Pull request number within the repository.
pullNumber.title: Pullnumber

reviewers.description: An array of user logins that will be removed.
reviewers.title: Reviewers

team_reviewers.description: An array of team slugs that will be removed. Omitted, null and [] mean none.
team_reviewers.title: Team Reviewers

tools.name: github_request_reviewers
tools.description: Requests reviews for a pull request from a given set of users and/or teams. Mirrors POST /repos/{o}/{r}/pulls/{n}/requested_reviewers: each new login or slug is added to the pull request's requested_reviewers / requested_teams and records a review_requested timeline event (review_requester, requested_reviewer or requested_team); one already requested is left as is. The pull request author is refused (Review cannot be requested from pull request author.) and so is a login with no account (Reviews may only be requested from collaborators. One or more of the users or teams you specified is not a collaborator of the {owner}/{repo} repository.), writing nothing; at least one of reviewers or team_reviewers is required. The answer is the updated pull request row.

pullNumber.description: Pull request number within the repository.
pullNumber.title: Pullnumber

reviewers.description: An array of user logins that will be requested. Each must be a known account and not the pull request author; omitted, null and [] mean none (then team_reviewers is required).
reviewers.title: Reviewers

team_reviewers.description: An array of team slugs that will be requested. Recorded verbatim and echoed as requested_teams (this server keeps no team roster).
team_reviewers.title: Team Reviewers

tools.name: github_search_code
tools.description: Search code across the indexed repositories; bare terms are ANDed (any order, no OR), a "double-quoted phrase" is matched exactly (contiguous, quotes stripped), `-` or `NOT` excludes. Supports `repo:`, `org:`, `user:`, `path:` (`/` = root, `dir` = repository-relative prefix), `filename:` (exact), `extension:`, `language:`, `size:`, `fork:`, `in:file|path|file,path`; a name:value token outside GitHub's search vocabulary is searched as text, a GitHub qualifier this tool does not support is rejected. Returns {total_count, incomplete_results, has_more, page, perPage, items} where items are per-file match rows, projected by `fields` when given.

query.description: Search terms matched against file contents (`in:file`, the default), file paths (`in:path`) or both (`in:file,path`). Terms are ANDed: every bare word must appear in the file, in any order; there is no OR operator; a token joined by punctuation (`src/app.py`, `auth-service`) is searched as its words. A "double-quoted phrase" must appear contiguously (quotes stripped). `-word`, `-"phrase"`, `NOT word` or `NOT "phrase"` excludes files containing it (a hyphen negates only before a letter; `-1` is a literal term). A term containing `://` is searched literally. Qualifiers: `repo:owner/name`, `org:`/`user:`, `path:/` (files at the repository root only), `path:dir` (that repository-relative directory and everything below it, case-insensitive), `filename:` (exact file name, case-insensitive), `extension:`, `language:`, `size:` (bytes, with `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=` or a range `A..B`), `fork:true|false|only`, `in:`. A query of only `filename:`, `path:` or `in:path` lists the matching files without a search term. A qualifier that takes one value may appear once (a second, different value is refused; `path:`, `filename:` and `in:` may repeat); two bounds are a range `A..B`. A token shaped like name:value whose name is not a GitHub search qualifier is searched as text; GitHub qualifiers this tool does not support are refused.
query.title: Query

perPage.description: Page size 1-100, default 30. A value below 1 is clamped to 1; a larger value is clamped to 100.
perPage.title: Perpage

fields.description: Subset of fields to return for each code search result. If omitted, all fields are returned. Use this to reduce response size when you only need specific fields; omitting 'repository' and 'text_matches' in particular drops the largest per-result data. Names: name, path, sha, repository, text_matches. path is always included; an empty or unknown name is refused.
fields.title: Fields

tools.name: github_search_commits
tools.description: Search commits by message; bare terms are ANDed (any order, no OR), a "double-quoted phrase" is matched exactly (contiguous, quotes stripped), `-` or `NOT` excludes. Mirrors GET /search/commits; supports repo:/org:/user:/author:/committer:/author-name:/committer-name:/author-email:/committer-email:/author-date:/committer-date:/hash:/merge: (author: and committer: also negated). Returns {total_count, incomplete_results, has_more, page, perPage, items} where items are commit rows carrying their repository, projected by `fields` when given. Newest authored first.

query.description: Search terms matched against commit messages. Terms are ANDed: every bare word must appear, in any order; there is no OR operator. A "double-quoted phrase" must appear contiguously (quotes stripped). `-word`, `-"phrase"` or `NOT word` excludes. Qualifiers: `repo:owner/name`, `org:`/`user:` (repository owner), `author:` and `committer:` (login or e-mail; `-author:`/`-committer:` exclude; repeats AND), `author-name:` and `committer-name:` (substring of the recorded name), `author-email:` and `committer-email:`, `author-date:` and `committer-date:` (YYYY-MM-DD or an ISO 8601 timestamp, with `>`, `>=`, `<`, `<=`, or a range `A..B` where either side may be `*`), `hash:` (a full sha or a prefix of 7+ hex characters, any case; two `hash:` tokens AND; with `repo:` a prefix that abbreviates two commits of that repository is refused), `merge:true|false` (decided per commit from its recorded parent links — a commit whose parents are not recorded matches neither; refused where no commit records any). tools.name: linear_create_attachment
tools.description: Attach a link or a small file to an issue and return {id, title, url}. Link form (url): the link joins the issue's links and is an attachment at once, listed by linear_get_attachments (kind "link") and readable by id through linear_get_attachment; url is the link. File form (base64Content + filename + contentType + sha256, optional size and subtitle): the decoded bytes must match sha256 (and size when given) and fit under 5000000 bytes, the file row is created on the issue (surface "upload"), the issue's updatedAt is stamped, and url is the file's upload asset URL. For larger files use linear_prepare_attachment_upload -> PUT -> linear_create_attachment_from_upload. Exactly one of url / base64Content must be given; every refusal writes nothing.

issueId.description: The issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123), in any case, to attach to.
issueId.title: Issueid

url.description: Link form: the link's absolute URL (scheme and host, no whitespace). A url already attached to the issue has its title updated under the same attachment id instead of being added twice. Give url or base64Content, never both.
url.title: Url

title.description: Optional title for the attachment: a link's title (the url itself when omitted or empty), a file's (the filename when omitted or empty).
title.title: Title

base64Content.description: Deprecated base64-encoded file content to upload. The one-call file form for small files: give it with filename, contentType and sha256 (never with url); the decoded bytes are checked against sha256 and size, and at most 5000000 bytes are accepted.
base64Content.title: Base64Content

filename.description: Filename for the upload (e.g., 'screenshot.png'). Required with base64Content.
filename.title: Filename

contentType.description: MIME type for the upload (e.g., 'image/png', 'application/pdf'). Required with base64Content; it decides the row's kind (image/*, audio/*, archives, else file).
contentType.title: Contenttype

sha256.description: Expected SHA-256 hex digest of the decoded file bytes. Required with base64Content; a mismatch refuses the call.
sha256.title: Sha256

size.description: Optional expected decoded file size in bytes. Rejects the upload if it does not match.
size.title: Size

subtitle.description: Optional subtitle for the attachment (file form).
subtitle.title: Subtitle

tools.name: linear_create_attachment_from_upload
tools.description: Step 3 of the file upload (after linear_prepare_attachment_upload and the PUT): create the attachment row from the prepared upload and return {id, title, url}. The row is created whether or not the PUT happened (a file with no bytes answers linear_get_attachment with truncated=true, reason "bytes_not_uploaded"); the pending upload is consumed and the issue's updatedAt is stamped. An assetUrl not on the Linear upload hosts is refused; one prepared for a different issue is refused naming that issue. One with no pending upload (never prepared, or already finalized) updates the attachment already carrying that URL on the issue — title and subtitle when given, same id — or, when there is none, creates a content-less row named by its last path segment. title defaults to the last path segment of assetUrl.

issue.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123), in any case: the issue the upload was prepared for.
issue.title: Issue

assetUrl.description: Linear upload assetUrl returned by linear_prepare_attachment_upload (a URL on uploads.linear.app or uploads.linear.dev; its last path segment names the upload).
assetUrl.title: Asseturl

title.description: Attachment title. Defaults to filename or asset URL (the last path segment of assetUrl).
title.title: Title

subtitle.description: Optional attachment subtitle; the one suggested at prepare time when omitted.
subtitle.title: Subtitle

tools.name: linear_create_comment
tools.description: Create a comment on an issue (issueId), or reply to an existing comment by passing parentId alone (the reply lands in the parent's thread, on the parent's issue).

body.description: The content of the comment as Markdown; stored verbatim, the empty string included.
body.title: Body

issueId.description: The issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123), in any case, to comment on. Required unless parentId is given; not consulted when it is, since a reply always lands on its parent's issue.
issueId.title: Issueid

parentId.description: A parent comment ID to reply to; issueId may then be omitted. The parent must be an existing comment; the reply joins the parent's thread on the parent's issue, and a reply to a reply is attached to the thread's top-level comment, so threads stay one level deep.
parentId.title: Parentid

tools.name: linear_create_issue
tools.description: Create a new issue in the Linear workspace. Every label must already exist and not be retired (linear_create_issue_label adds one, linear_restore_issue_label brings a retired one back); an unknown or retired label refuses the call and writes nothing. blockedBy / blocks / relatedTo / duplicateOf record relations to existing issues (read back with linear_get_issue includeRelations); an entry naming no issue refuses the call with issue_not_found, and a duplicate-type state needs duplicateOf.

title.description: The issue title. An empty or whitespace-only title is refused.
title.title: Title

assignee.description: The user to assign (User ID, name, email, or "me"). An empty string is refused, not read as no assignee; omit the field instead.
assignee.title: Assignee

project.description: The project name or ID to add the issue to; the issue's team joins that project's teams when not among them. An empty string is refused, not read as no project; omit the field instead.
project.title: Project

parentId.description: The parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case), if this is a sub-issue.
parentId.title: Parentid

priority.description: The issue priority (0=None, 1=Urgent, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low). Only 0-4 is accepted; anything else is refused and nothing is written.
priority.title: Priority

state.description: The issue state type, name, or ID, resolved against the team's workflow states (see linear_list_issue_statuses); an unknown value fails the call. Omitted: the team's first backlog state (else its first unstarted state, else the first state in its workflow), or the duplicate-type state when duplicateOf is given. A duplicate-type state can only be moved into when the issue has a duplicate relation (duplicateOf, in this call or before); otherwise the call is refused with invalid_input and nothing is written.
state.title: State

dueDate.description: The due date for the issue in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD; a date-time is stored as its calendar day). Anything unparsable is refused.
dueDate.title: Duedate

estimate.description: The numerical issue estimate value, 0 or more; a negative value is refused and nothing is written. On create, pass null or omit for no estimate.
estimate.title: Estimate

cycle.description: The cycle name, number, or ID to add the issue to.
cycle.title: Cycle

labels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Improvement"]) to set on the issue. Each entry must be an existing, non-retired label name or ID, in any case, among the workspace's labels and the team's own (see linear_list_issue_labels; linear_create_issue_label creates one), and the issue stores the label's own spelling ("bug" stores "Bug"); a team label sharing a workspace label's name is retired-checked as the workspace label, since its stored name is read as that one. An unresolved entry refuses the whole call with label_not_found, a retired one with label_retired, and nothing is written. Omitted means no labels.
labels.title: Labels

links.description: Link attachments to add, as [{"url", "title"}]: both required, url an absolute URL. Append-only: this field never removes a link (linear_delete_attachment does), and each link becomes an attachment with its own id (see linear_get_attachments).
links.title: Links

blockedBy.description: Issue IDs/identifiers blocking this. Append-only; existing relations are never removed. Each entry is an issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case); the first entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is created; repeats collapse to one.
blockedBy.title: Blockedby

blocks.description: Issue IDs/identifiers this blocks. Append-only; existing relations are never removed. Each entry is an issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case); the first entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is created; repeats collapse to one.
blocks.title: Blocks

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed. A related pair reads the same from both issues. Each entry is an issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case); the first entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is created; repeats collapse to one.
relatedTo.title: Relatedto

duplicateOf.description: Duplicate of issue ID/identifier. Records one duplicate relation and, unless state is given, creates the issue in its team's duplicate-type state (canceled_at stamped). An unresolvable value refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is created.
duplicateOf.title: Duplicateof

tools.name: linear_create_issue_label
tools.description: Create an issue label in the workspace, or in one team with team, and return the new label row {id, name, color, description, team_id, created_at, updated_at, retired_at}. The label is usable at once on linear_create_issue / linear_update_issue and listed by linear_list_issue_labels. A name already used by a label in the same scope (any case, a retired one included) is refused and nothing is written; linear_update_issue_label changes a label, linear_retire_issue_label / linear_restore_issue_label retire and bring one back.

name.description: The label's name, trimmed; required. Unique in its scope in any case: a name a workspace label already spells (or, with team, one of that team's labels spells) is refused.
name.title: Name

team.description: Optional team name, key, or ID (any case) to scope the label to; only that team's issues may carry it. Omit for a workspace label, which any issue may carry. An empty string is refused, not read as the workspace.
team.title: Team

color.description: Optional hex colour as #RRGGBB (e.g. "#5E6AD2"); anything else is refused and nothing is written.
color.title: Color

description.description: Optional free-text description of the label.
description.title: Description

tools.name: linear_create_project
tools.description: Create a new project in the Linear workspace. `state` is resolved against the workspace's project statuses (type word, name or id) and an unknown value fails the call; omitted, the project lands in the backlog-type status. team leads the project and addTeams share it with more teams (teams[] lists them all); a started / completed / canceled-type state stamps startedAt / completedAt / canceledAt now; links adds external resource links, counted by resourceCount.

name.description: A descriptive name of the project.
name.title: Name

description.description: The full project description in Markdown format.
description.title: Description

summary.description: A concise plaintext summary of the project (max 255 chars); a longer one is refused and nothing is written.
summary.title: Summary

lead.description: The user to assign as lead (User ID, name, email, or "me"). An empty string is refused, not read as no lead; omit the field instead.
lead.title: Lead

priority.description: The priority of the project (0=None, 1=Urgent, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low). Only 0-4 is accepted; anything else is refused and nothing is written.
priority.title: Priority

state.description: The project status: a type word (backlog, planned, started, paused, completed, canceled), a status name in any case (Backlog, Planned, In Progress, Paused, Completed, Canceled unless the workspace defines others) or a status id; the status's name is stored as state. Matched as id, then name, then type word, so a status itself named with a type word (a legacy 'started') wins over the type-word reading. An unknown value fails the call with state_not_found listing the statuses and nothing is written. Omitted or empty: the first backlog-type status.
state.title: State

startDate.description: The start date of the project in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD; a date-time is stored as its calendar day). Anything unparsable is refused.
startDate.title: Startdate

targetDate.description: The target date of the project in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD; a date-time is stored as its calendar day). Anything unparsable is refused.
targetDate.title: Targetdate

labels.description: Array of labels to set on the project.
labels.title: Labels

addTeams.description: Additional teams to share the project with (team name, key or ID each); team stays the lead team and is always among the project's teams. An unknown team fails the call with team_not_found and nothing is written.
addTeams.title: Addteams

icon.description: Icon name or emoji code (e.g. "Rocket" or ":eagle:"), not a raw Unicode emoji; at most 64 characters. Anything longer, or a raw emoji, is refused as invalid_input and nothing is written.
icon.title: Icon

color.description: Hex color (#RRGGBB, stored lower-cased); omitted, the project takes the default #bec2c8. Anything else is refused as invalid_input and nothing is written.
color.title: Color

startDateResolution.description: Start date resolution: one of halfYear, month, quarter, year, saying how precise startDate is; omit for a precise day. Anything else is refused as invalid_input and nothing is written.
startDateResolution.title: Startdateresolution

targetDateResolution.description: Target date resolution: one of halfYear, month, quarter, year, saying how precise targetDate is; omit for a precise day. Anything else is refused as invalid_input and nothing is written.
targetDateResolution.title: Targetdateresolution

links.description: External resource links to add, as [{"url", "title"}]: both required, url an absolute URL. Append-only: this field never removes a link; a url already on the project updates that link's title under the same id. Counted by resourceCount and listed by linear_get_project(includeResources=true) as resources [{type, id, label, url}].
links.title: Links

tools.name: linear_get_attachment
tools.description: Get an attachment. With format "content" (the default) a file's bytes are returned as an MCP EmbeddedResource (handled as a file, not LLM text) when the file is <= 5 MB; larger files return metadata with truncated=true and abs_path so the harness reads them directly, and a file finalized before its bytes were uploaded returns metadata with truncated=true and reason "bytes_not_uploaded". A link attachment returns its metadata (id, title, url) with no bytes. With format "url" every attachment answers {id, title, url}: a file's url is its upload asset URL (an opaque key, not fetchable), a link's is the link itself.

format.description: Response format. Defaults to content. "content" returns the metadata with a file's bytes; "url" returns {id, title, url} for any attachment (a file's upload asset URL, a link's url). Anything else is refused.
format.title: Format

tools.name: linear_get_attachments
tools.description: List an issue's attachments with metadata: files (kind image, audio, archive or file: id, filename, kind, mime_type, size, surface, title, subtitle, url) and links (kind "link": id, title, url). Fetch file bytes with linear_get_attachment.

issueId.description: The issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123), in any case.
issueId.title: Issueid

tools.name: linear_get_issue
tools.description: Get a specific issue, optionally capping the description length; includeRelations adds its relations object (blocks, blockedBy, relatedTo, duplicateOf), which linear_create_issue / linear_update_issue write through blockedBy / blocks / relatedTo / duplicateOf and the remove* arguments; the row carries uuid and attachments [{id, title, subtitle, url}] (files and links; linear_get_attachments has the full metadata).

id.description: Issue ID, identifier (e.g., ENG-123) in any case, or the issue's uuid.
id.title: Id

maxDescriptionChars.description: Truncate the description to this many characters; 0 omits it entirely. Omit for the full text.
maxDescriptionChars.title: Maxdescriptionchars

includeRelations.description: Include blocking/related/duplicate relations: with true the row gains `relations` {blocks, blockedBy, relatedTo, duplicateOf}, each entry {id, title} with id the other issue's identifier (blocks: issues this one blocks; blockedBy: issues blocking it; duplicateOf: one entry or null). Default false leaves the key out; list rows never carry it.
includeRelations.title: Includerelations

tools.name: linear_get_job_result

query.title: Query

team.description: The team name, key, or ID whose workflow states to list. Required.

limit.description: The number of results to return (1-250). A value outside that range is refused as an invalid argument.

tools.name: linear_update_issue
tools.description: Update an existing issue in the Linear workspace. description replaces the whole text; patch edits the current description in place (replace / insert_before / insert_after / prepend / append / replace_range, applied in order, all or nothing, every anchor matching exactly once) and is the way to edit a long one — the two cannot be combined. labels replaces the whole label set; addLabels / removeLabels change it incrementally; every entry must be an existing label name or ID (linear_create_issue_label adds one), an unknown one refuses the call and writes nothing, and a retired label can be kept or removed but not applied to an issue that lacks it. A label argument that leaves the stored list as it is changes nothing and does not move updatedAt. labels replaces the whole label set; addLabels / removeLabels change it incrementally; every entry must be an existing label name or ID (linear_create_issue_label adds one), an unknown one refuses the call and writes nothing, and a retired label can be kept or removed but not applied to an issue that lacks it. A label argument that leaves the stored list as it is changes nothing and does not move updatedAt. blockedBy / blocks / relatedTo add relations and removeBlockedBy / removeBlocks / removeRelatedTo remove them (read back with linear_get_issue includeRelations); duplicateOf marks the issue a duplicate and moves it to the duplicate-type state, null clears it; an entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found, one naming this issue is skipped and listed under warnings, and a duplicate-type state is refused without a duplicate relation.

id.description: Issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123), in any case.
id.title: Id

title.description: The issue title. An empty or whitespace-only title is refused.
title.title: Title

description.description: The issue description as Markdown. Replaces the whole stored text; use patch to edit part of it. Cannot be combined with patch.
description.title: Description

old_string.description: Exact text to replace. Must match the current content exactly once

new_string.description: Replacement text. Empty string deletes the match

replace_all.description: Replace every occurrence instead of requiring a unique match

anchor.description: Exact text to insert before. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly before the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")

anchor.description: Exact text to insert after. Must match the current content exactly once

text.description: Text to insert directly after the anchor. Include separators (e.g. "\n\n")
Text to insert at the very start of the content
Text to insert at the very end of the content

from.description: Exact text where the range starts (inclusive). Must match exactly once

to.description: Exact text where the range ends (exclusive, stays in place). Must match exactly once after `from`

new_string.description: Text replacing the range. Empty string deletes it

patch.description: Partial edits applied to the current description, in order and atomically (one failing operation aborts the whole save and nothing is written). Every anchor string must match the current content exactly once; replace with replace_all is the one exception. Only valid on update, in place of the full description field, and cannot be combined with it. The way to edit a long description: ops are replace {old_string, new_string, replace_all?}, insert_before / insert_after {anchor, text}, prepend / append {text}, replace_range {from, to, new_string} (from inclusive, to exclusive and kept); an empty new_string deletes. 1-50 ops; a failure is invalid_input "Patch failed, nothing was saved. Operation N (<op>): <detail>" and a multi-match lists the matching locations (up to 20) with 25 characters of context. A successful patch stamps updated_at even when the text ends up unchanged.
patch.title: Patch

assignee.description: The user to assign (User ID, name, email, or "me"). Pass null to remove; omit to leave unchanged. An empty string is refused, not read as no assignee.
assignee.title: Assignee

project.description: The project name or ID to add the issue to; the issue's team joins that project's teams when not among them. Pass null to remove; omit to leave unchanged. An empty string is refused, not read as no project.

parentId.description: The parent issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case), if this is a sub-issue. The issue itself, or one of its own sub-issues at any depth, is refused. Pass null to remove; omit to leave unchanged.

priority.description: The issue priority (0=None, 1=Urgent, 2=High, 3=Medium, 4=Low). Only 0-4 is accepted; anything else is refused and nothing is written.

state.description: The issue state type, name, or ID, resolved against the issue's team workflow states (see linear_list_issue_statuses); an unknown value fails the call and writes nothing. started_at / completed_at / canceled_at follow the new state's type (set on entry, cleared on leaving; re-entry restores the original) and the transition is appended to state_history. A duplicate-type state can only be moved into when the issue has a duplicate relation (duplicateOf, in this call or before); otherwise the call is refused with invalid_input and nothing is written. Writing the issue's current state again is not a move and is not checked.
state.title: State

dueDate.description: The due date for the issue in ISO format (YYYY-MM-DD; a date-time is stored as its calendar day). Anything unparsable is refused. On update, pass null to remove the due date.

Cannot be combined with addLabels/removeLabels; prefer those for incremental changes. Each entry must be an existing label name or ID, in any case, among the workspace's labels and the issue's team's own (see linear_list_issue_labels; linear_create_issue_label creates one), a team label sharing a workspace label's name being retired-checked as the workspace label its stored name is read as; an unresolved entry refuses the whole call with label_not_found, a retired label the issue does not already carry with label_retired, and nothing is written.

removeLabels.description: Label names or IDs as a JSON array of strings (e.g. ["Bug", "Improvement"]) to remove. Only valid when updating an existing issue. Cannot be combined with labels. Each entry is an issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case); the first entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is written, an entry naming this issue is skipped and reported under `warnings`, and one that changes nothing does not move updated_at.

Each entry is an issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case); the first entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is written, an entry naming this issue is skipped and reported under `warnings`, and one that changes nothing does not move updated_at.

relatedTo.description: Related issue IDs/identifiers. Append-only; existing relations are never removed (removeRelatedTo does). A related pair reads the same from both issues. Each entry is an issue ID or identifier (e.g., ENG-123, any case); the first entry naming no issue refuses the whole call with issue_not_found and nothing is written, an entry naming this issue is skipped and reported under `warnings`, and one that changes nothing does not move updated_at.

tools.name: trello_search
tools.description: Trello-style universal search (GET /1/search) over actions, boards, cards, members and organizations, with Trello's card operators (@member, #label, list:, board:, is:, has:, due:, created:, edited:, name:/description:/comment:/checklist:, sort:, leading - to negate). Card hits default to open cards, most-recently-active first, and carry cards_total so a cards_limit truncation is visible; cards_page walks the cards arm.

query.description: Trello search grammar. Free words are case-insensitive substrings of the arm's text (cards and boards: name or desc; members: fullName or username; organizations: name or displayName; actions: comment text) that must ALL match, in any order; quote a phrase ("password reset") to match it as one unit. Operators filter the cards arm only: is:open|archived (overrides cards_filter), @username / member:username (member:me = the claimed persona), #label / label:name-or-color (label:"Two Words"), list:name, board:name-or-id, due:day|week|month|N|overdue|complete|incomplete, created:day|week|month|N, edited:day|week|month|N, has:attachments|description|members|cover, name:/description:/comment:/checklist:text, sort:created|due|edited|-edited, and a leading - negates any word or operator (-has:members). #word, @name and a leading - are read as operators; quoting the phrase makes them literal text. An unknown prefix (C:\path, Spec:) is literal text; a known operator with a malformed or empty value is refused as invalid_value. An empty query matches nothing.
query.title: Query

modelTypes.description: Types to search over: "actions", "boards", "cards", "members", "organizations" — as a JSON array or a comma-separated string ("cards,boards"). Empty (the default) or "all" = all five. A value outside this set, or an empty token in the string, is refused as invalid_value. Every arm is always present in the result, empty when not requested or when nothing matched.
modelTypes.title: Modeltypes

idBoards.description: Restrict the cards, boards and actions arms to these board IDs — a JSON array or a comma-separated string — or "mine" for the boards whose roster holds the acting member (a claimed persona or the env actor; with only the default fallback actor "mine" restricts nothing). Empty = all boards; an empty token in the string is refused as invalid_value.
idBoards.title: Idboards

boards_limit.description: Max boards to return (1-100, default 10; Trello: default 10, max 1000). Out-of-range values are clamped, not refused.
boards_limit.title: Boards Limit

cards_limit.description: Max cards per page (1-500, default 50; Trello: default 10, max 1000). Out-of-range values are clamped, not refused.
cards_limit.title: Cards Limit

cards_filter.description: Card filter for the cards results — "open" (default, non-archived only), "closed" (archived only), "all" (open + archived), "visible" (= open), "none" (no cards), "complete" (open cards whose dueComplete is true) or "incomplete" (open cards whose dueComplete is false). An is:open / is:archived operator in the query overrides it. Any other value is refused as invalid_value. An explicit null means the same as omitting it.
cards_filter.title: Cards Filter

cards_page.description: Page of the cards arm, 0-100 (default 0; Trello's own ceiling is 100). The page size is cards_limit and cards_total is unchanged, so page N is cards N*cards_limit onward. Negative, non-integer or >100 values are refused as invalid_value; a page past the end is an empty cards arm.
cards_page.title: Cards Page

partial.description: Accepted for parity with GET /1/search and has no effect: matching here is already a per-word substring, at least as wide as Trello's partial=true prefix match. Must be a JSON boolean.

Case-insensitive. Any other value, the empty string included, is rejected with a 400 error. Default 'full'.

Omitted or empty keeps the envelope: From, To, Cc, Bcc, Reply-To, Date, Subject, List-Id. Ask by name for the rest (Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References, Content-Type, Received, ...); ["*"] keeps every header (Gmail's own default; 50+ transport and anti-spam headers on ingested mail). user_email.title: User Email

format.description: How much of each message to return, as on gmail_get_message: 'minimal' (ids, labels and snippet), 'metadata' (headers filtered to metadata_headers, no body; the default here, about 1 KB per message), or 'full' (everything; about 12 KB per ingested message, so at most 10 ids per call). Case-insensitive. Any other value, the empty string included, is rejected with a 400 error. Default 'full'. The whole thread is returned whatever the format, so pick 'metadata' or 'minimal' for a long one.

metadata_headers.description: With format='metadata', which headers to keep on each message, by name, case-insensitively, in the message's own order.
