tools.description: Search messages in a mailbox with the Gmail search-box grammar (users.messages.list with q); returns id/threadId pairs newest first.

query.description: Gmail search-box query (users.messages.list q). Operators: from: to: cc: bcc: (me = this mailbox; a full address matches exactly; @domain; or a name/address fragment), subject:, label: (label NAME or id), category: (primary|social|promotions|updates|forums|reservations|purchases; the last two name the mailbox's user label of that name), has:attachment|userlabels|nouserlabels, filename:, in: (inbox|sent|drafts|trash|spam|archive|anywhere), is: (unread|read|starred|important), after:/before:/older:/newer: (YYYY/MM/DD, MM/DD/YYYY or epoch seconds; midnight in the mailbox's zone), older_than:/newer_than: (7d, 3m, 1y), size:/larger:/smaller:, rfc822msgid:, deliveredto:, list:. `OR` or {a b} = any-of, (a b) or op:(a b) = all-of, -x negates, "phrase", +word = exact word; free text matches subject, body and sender/recipient names. SPAM/TRASH excluded unless the query names them. A malformed value, an unknown label, or an unmodelled operator (AROUND, has:drive, in:snoozed, is:muted) is a 400 naming it, never silently dropped.
query.title: Query

user_email.description: Mailbox to search. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

page_token.description: Opaque cursor from a prior call, exactly as returned in nextPageToken. A value this tool never issued (including a bare number) is refused as an invalid argument, not read as the first page.
page_token.title: Page Token

tools.name: gmail_send_draft
tools.description:
Send an existing draft. Mirrors POST /users/{userId}/drafts/send.

Every To/Cc/Bcc address of the draft becomes a contact, minus the
owning mailbox's own: a draft to yourself sends and lands in Sent, and
mints no contact.

draft_id.description: Draft message ID to send. Its To/Cc/Bcc addresses become contacts on send, except the owning mailbox's own: a draft to yourself still lands in Sent but mints no contact.
draft_id.title: Draft Id

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the draft. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

tools.name: gmail_send_message
tools.description: Send an email (mirrors users.messages.send): the SENT copy is written here and a copy lands in every recipient mailbox this universe holds, in the same conversation, stamped Delivered-To with that recipient.

to.description: Recipient email addresses. Any non-empty To/Cc/Bcc set sends (a Bcc-only mailing is fine). Each address becomes a contact, except the sending mailbox's own: a note-to-self lands in Sent and Inbox and mints no contact. A recipient whose mailbox is in this universe receives a copy in their INBOX, in the same conversation.
to.title: To

body.description: Plain-text message body.
body.title: Body

cc.description: Cc recipients; each becomes a contact, the sender's own address excepted, and receives a copy when their mailbox is in this universe.
cc.title: Cc

bcc.description: Bcc recipients; each becomes a contact, the sender's own address excepted, and receives a copy (without the Bcc list) when their mailbox is in this universe.
bcc.title: Bcc

thread_id.description: Existing thread to post into, matched exactly in this mailbox; omit to start a new conversation. An empty string is refused with 400, not read as omitted.
thread_id.title: Thread Id

user_email.description: Mailbox to send from. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

html_body.description: Optional HTML body, served as the text/html alternative beside the plain-text body (the plain text is derived from the HTML when body is empty).
html_body.title: Html Body

attachments.description: Optional attachments: objects {filename, mime_type, data_b64} with the bytes base64url-encoded (the standard alphabet and missing padding are accepted). The filename is reduced to its basename ('.' and '..' are refused). Each becomes an attachment part with an attachmentId that gmail_get_attachment serves, and filename:/has:attachment find it.
attachments.title: Attachments

headers.description: Optional extra headers as objects {name, value} (X-Priority, Reply-To, ...). From, To, Cc, Bcc, Subject, Date, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References and Delivered-To are set by the message itself and are refused with 400.
headers.title: Headers

tools.name: gmail_submit_search_messages
tools.description: Submit a message search for async execution; poll gmail_get_job_status then gmail_get_job_result.

query.description: Gmail search-box query (users.messages.list q). Operators: from: to: cc: bcc: (me = this mailbox; a full address matches exactly; @domain; or a name/address fragment), subject:, label: (label NAME or id), category: (primary|social|promotions|updates|forums|reservations|purchases; the last two name the mailbox's user label of that name), has:attachment|userlabels|nouserlabels, filename:, in: (inbox|sent|drafts|trash|spam|archive|anywhere), is: (unread|read|starred|important), after:/before:/older:/newer: (YYYY/MM/DD, MM/DD/YYYY or epoch seconds; midnight in the mailbox's zone), older_than:/newer_than: (7d, 3m, 1y), size:/larger:/smaller:, rfc822msgid:, deliveredto:, list:. `OR` or {a b} = any-of, (a b) or op:(a b) = all-of, -x negates, "phrase", +word = exact word; free text matches subject, body and sender/recipient names. SPAM/TRASH excluded unless the query names them. A malformed value, an unknown label, or an unmodelled operator (AROUND, has:drive, in:snoozed, is:muted) is a 400 naming it, never silently dropped.
query.title: Query

user_email.description: Mailbox to search. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

page_token.description: Opaque cursor from a prior call, exactly as returned in nextPageToken. A value this tool never issued (including a bare number) is refused as an invalid argument, not read as the first page.
page_token.title: Page Token

tools.name: gmail_trash_message
tools.description: Move a message to TRASH (reversible via gmail_untrash_message).

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the message. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

tools.name: gmail_trash_thread
tools.description:
Move all messages in a thread to TRASH (reversible via untrash_thread).
Returns a status summary, not the thread: its labelIds is the UNION across the thread's messages, so read per-message state back with gmail_get_thread.

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the thread. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

tools.name: gmail_untrash_message
tools.description: Restore a trashed message.

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the message. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

tools.name: gmail_untrash_thread
tools.description:
Restore a trashed thread.
Returns a status summary, not the thread: its labelIds is the UNION across the thread's messages, so read per-message state back with gmail_get_thread.

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the thread. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

tools.name: gmail_update_draft
tools.description: Edit a draft in place (mirrors users.drafts.update): same id and thread, the draft moves to the top of gmail_list_drafts, omitted fields keep their stored value; answers the Draft resource {id, message}.

draft_id.description: Draft ID to edit (the id gmail_create_draft and gmail_list_drafts report).
draft_id.title: Draft Id

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the draft. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

to.description: New To recipients; omit to keep the stored ones, pass [] to clear them.
to.title: To

cc.description: New Cc recipients; omit to keep, [] to clear.
cc.title: Cc

bcc.description: New Bcc recipients; omit to keep, [] to clear.
bcc.title: Bcc

subject.description: New subject; omit to keep, '' to clear.
subject.title: Subject

body.description: New plain-text body; omit to keep, '' to clear.
body.title: Body

html_body.description: Optional HTML body, served as the text/html alternative beside the plain-text body (the plain text is derived from the HTML when body is empty). Omit to keep the stored HTML, '' to drop it.
html_body.title: Html Body

attachments.description: Optional attachments: objects {filename, mime_type, data_b64} with the bytes base64url-encoded (the standard alphabet and missing padding are accepted). The filename is reduced to its basename ('.' and '..' are refused). Each becomes an attachment part with an attachmentId that gmail_get_attachment serves, and filename:/has:attachment find it. Omit to keep the stored attachments; a list replaces them ([] removes all).
attachments.title: Attachments

headers.description: Optional extra headers as objects {name, value} (X-Priority, Reply-To, ...). From, To, Cc, Bcc, Subject, Date, Message-ID, In-Reply-To, References and Delivered-To are set by the message itself and are refused with 400. Omit to keep the stored extra headers; a list replaces them.
headers.title: Headers

tools.name: gmail_update_label
tools.description: Rename, recolour or change the visibility of a user label in place (mirrors users.labels.patch); the id is unchanged, so every message keeps the label.

label_id.description: Gmail label ID of a user label this mailbox holds (Label_...). A system or category label is refused with 400; an id this mailbox does not hold is 404.
label_id.title: Label Id

user_email.description: Mailbox owning the label. 'me' names the acting mailbox, as userId='me' does on the API.
user_email.title: User Email

name.description: New label name. A name this mailbox already holds under another id, or a system label's name, is refused with 409.
name.title: Name

text_color.description: New text colour from Gmail's fixed label palette; set together with background_color. Any other value is a 400.
text_color.title: Text Color

background_color.description: New background colour from Gmail's fixed label palette; set together with text_color.
background_color.title: Background Color

clear_color.description: Remove the label's colour. Ignored when a colour is given.
clear_color.title: Clear Color

message_list_visibility.description: 'show' | 'hide'. Any other value is a 400. Omitted keeps the current value.
message_list_visibility.title: Message List Visibility

label_list_visibility.description: 'labelShow' | 'labelShowIfUnread' | 'labelHide'. Any other value is a 400. Omitted keeps the current value.
label_list_visibility.title: Label List Visibility

tools.name: gcal_clear_calendar
tools.description: Delete every event on a primary calendar — one-offs, recurring masters and their overrides, cancelled rows included — leaving the calendar itself, its sharing and every calendar list entry as they were. Only the calendar's owner may clear it (403 otherwise); nobody is mailed. Answers {cleared, calendarId, summary, eventsDeleted}.

calendarId.description: The primary calendar to clear, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar. Only a primary calendar (the persona's own, whose id is their address) can be cleared; a secondary is refused with 400 "Cannot clear primary calendar" (the vendor's own wording for that refusal) — delete it with gcal_delete_calendar or its events with gcal_delete_event.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

tools.name: gcal_create_event
tools.description: Create an event on a calendar. "primary" is the acting user's own calendar, which every known persona has (its id is their address) even on a universe that seeded no calendars. Attendees are recorded on the event and mailed the invitation when sendUpdates is all or externalOnly; no copy is placed on an attendee's own calendar, so a guest with no calendar in this universe is not an error.

calendarId.description: The calendar ID to create the event on, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

event.description: Event resource: {summary, description, location, start: {dateTime|date, timeZone}, end: {...}, attendees: [{email, responseStatus?}], recurrence: ["RRULE:..."], status, visibility, transparency, id?}. A dateTime without a UTC offset requires an IANA timeZone and is returned with the offset of that zone. start and end are required and must both be timed or both be all-day (an all-day end.date is exclusive, so a one-day event ends the next day). Recurring events set recurrence (RFC 5545 RRULE/EXRULE/RDATE/EXDATE lines; rrule is an accepted alias that must agree when both are given; DTSTART/DTEND lines are refused) and a timed recurring master needs start.timeZone. status is one of confirmed, tentative, cancelled; visibility one of default, public, private, confidential; transparency one of opaque, transparent; sequence a non-negative integer. Every attendee is an object with an email and, optionally, displayName, responseStatus (needsAction, accepted, declined, tentative), optional, organizer, self, resource, comment, additionalGuests and id; any other attendee key is refused. reminders, colorId, guestsCanInviteOthers, guestsCanModify, guestsCanSeeOtherGuests, extendedProperties, conferenceData, attachments, source, eventType, anyoneCanAddSelf, attendeesOmitted and privateCopy are stored as given and echoed back. iCalUID (or ical_uid) is honoured on create and ignored on update and patch. The read-only fields an event just read carries (kind, etag, htmlLink, created, updated, organizer, creator, hangoutLink, recurringEventId, originalStartTime, endTimeUnspecified, locked, and the snake_case recurring_event_id and original_start_time) are ignored, so a read event can be re-sent as it came. Any other key is refused with 400 and invalid_fields naming it. Whenever at least one guest is listed the organizer is listed among the attendees too, with organizer: true (responseStatus accepted unless the body gives theirs); attendees[].self is read-only on the wire: the entry whose email is the calendar id carries it. An id (or event_id) you supply must be 5-1024 base32hex characters (a-v, 0-9), else 400 Invalid resource id value. Refused with 400: a dateTime with no offset and no timeZone, a timeZone that is not an IANA key, a dateTime with no offset naming a wall time its timeZone skips at a daylight-saving transition, and an end before the start. Refused with 409: an id another event on the calendar already holds. Checks run in the order calendar 404, permission 403, body 400, taken id 409. Nothing is written on any refusal.
event.title: Event

sendUpdates.description: Who is mailed about this write: "all" every guest, "externalOnly" only the guests this universe's directory does not know (no calendar, contacts persona or mailbox here — the people outside the workspace, not an email-domain test), "none" nobody. Default none, as on the real API. RSVP mail to the organizer is not governed by this.
sendUpdates.title: Sendupdates

tools.name: gcal_delete_acl
tools.description: Revoke a rule (the real acl.delete): the rule is kept with role none, so gcal_list_acl with showDeleted still shows it and a later gcal_insert_acl for the same principal revives it. The principal loses whatever that rule granted; a user who still qualifies through a domain or default rule keeps that role. The calendar owner's own user rule cannot be removed (403 "Cannot change the owner's access to the calendar."). Only the calendar's owner may change access (403 otherwise); an unknown or already deleted rule is 404 "Not Found". Nobody is mailed. Answers {deleted, calendarId, ruleId}.

calendarId.description: The calendar whose access control list this names, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar. A calendar that does not exist or that the acting user cannot read is 404 "Calendar not found: <calendarId>", exactly as on every read.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

ruleId.description: The ACL rule identifier exactly as gcal_list_acl reports it in id: "user:<email>", "group:<email>", "domain:<domain>" or "default". A rule the calendar does not carry, or one already deleted, is 404 "Not Found".
ruleId.title: Ruleid

tools.name: gcal_delete_calendar
tools.description: Delete a secondary calendar together with every event on it. Only the calendar's owner may delete it (403 otherwise); a primary calendar — the persona's own, whose id is their address — is refused with 400 "Cannot delete primary calendar": delete its events instead. Nobody is mailed. Answers {deleted, calendarId, summary, eventsDeleted}.

calendarId.description: The calendar ID to delete. "primary" resolves to the acting user's own calendar and is then refused: only a secondary calendar can be deleted.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

tools.name: gcal_delete_calendar_list_entry
tools.description: Remove a calendar from the acting user's calendar list without touching its sharing: the entry is kept as deleted (visible to gcal_list_calendars with showDeleted) and the calendar itself, its events and every other user's list are unchanged. A calendar not on the list — unreadable, or already removed — is 404. Answers {deleted, calendarId, summary}. Requires an acting user.

calendarId.description: The calendar ID to remove from the acting user's calendar list, or "primary" for their own calendar, which is then refused: the primary calendar cannot be removed from the list. Removing an entry never changes who may read or write the calendar — gcal_get_calendar and the event tools keep working on it, and gcal_insert_calendar_list_entry puts it back.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

tools.name: gcal_delete_event
tools.description: Delete an event (soft-delete by default).

calendarId.description: The calendar ID containing the event, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

hardDelete.description: If true, remove the row; default soft-deletes via status=cancelled. An instance or override of a recurring event is only ever cancelled, since removing it would bring the occurrence back. Deleting an event that is already cancelled answers 410 Resource has been deleted and mails nobody, unless hardDelete removes a cancelled one-off or master.
hardDelete.title: Harddelete

sendUpdates.description: Who is mailed about this write: "all" every guest, "externalOnly" only the guests this universe's directory does not know (no calendar, contacts persona or mailbox here — the people outside the workspace, not an email-domain test), "none" nobody. Default none, as on the real API. RSVP mail to the organizer is not governed by this.
sendUpdates.title: Sendupdates

tools.name: gcal_freebusy_query
tools.description: Query free/busy windows across one or more calendars.

calendarIds.description: List of calendar IDs to query free/busy windows for; "primary" stands for the acting user's own calendar.
calendarIds.title: Calendarids

timeMin.description: Start of the query window: lower bound on the event's end time, EXCLUSIVE (a busy block ending exactly at timeMin is not reported). Must be an RFC 3339 timestamp with a time zone offset or Z (e.g. 2026-09-12T00:00:00Z); fractional seconds are ignored. A date-only, offset-less or empty value is refused with a 400 naming the parameter. timeMin must be smaller than timeMax, else 400 "The specified time range is empty."
timeMin.title: Timemin

timeMax.description: End of the query window: upper bound on the event's start time, EXCLUSIVE (a busy block starting exactly at timeMax is not reported). Must be an RFC 3339 timestamp with a time zone offset or Z (e.g. 2026-09-13T00:00:00Z); fractional seconds are ignored. A date-only, offset-less or empty value is refused with a 400 naming the parameter. timeMin must be smaller than timeMax, else 400 "The specified time range is empty."
timeMax.title: Timemax

tools.name: gcal_get_acl
tools.description: Return one access control rule of a calendar as {kind: "calendar#aclRule", etag, id, scope: {type, value}, role}. Requires writer or owner on the calendar: a reader or writerWithoutPrivateAccess is 403, a calendar the acting user cannot read is 404 Calendar not found; a deleted rule is 404 "Not Found" like a rule that never existed.

calendarId.description: The calendar whose access control list this names, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar. A calendar that does not exist or that the acting user cannot read is 404 "Calendar not found: <calendarId>", exactly as on every read.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

ruleId.description: The ACL rule identifier exactly as gcal_list_acl reports it in id: "user:<email>", "group:<email>", "domain:<domain>" or "default". A rule the calendar does not carry, or one already deleted, is 404 "Not Found".
ruleId.title: Ruleid

tools.name: gcal_get_calendar
tools.description: Get a single calendar.

calendarId.description: The calendar ID to fetch, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

tools.name: gcal_get_colors
tools.description: The colour palette for calendars and events: {kind: "calendar#colors", updated, calendar: {id: {background, foreground}}, event: {id: {background, foreground}}}. calendar ids are what colorId means on a calendar list entry (gcal_patch_calendar_list_entry) and event ids what colorId means on an event; backgroundColor/foregroundColor on a list entry are looked up here. Static and identical for every user.

tools.name: gcal_get_event
tools.description: Get a single event.

calendarId.description: The calendar ID containing the event, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

tools.name: gcal_get_setting
tools.description: Read one of the acting user's settings. Answers {kind: "calendar#setting", etag, id, value}. Requires an acting user who owns a primary calendar ("primary" must resolve): with no acting user 400 Invalid Value, with no primary 404.

setting.description: The id of the user setting to read. Only "timezone" exists here: the acting user's time zone, which is their primary calendar's timeZone (gcal_patch_calendar("primary", {"timeZone": …}) changes it). The vendor's other settings (locale, format24HourTime, weekStart, …) are not modelled and are refused by the argument guard. On a universe built from a Takeout export the zone is the universe's default_time_zone, so every persona reads the same value.
setting.title: Setting

tools.name: gcal_import_event
tools.description: Import a private copy of an existing event onto a calendar, keyed by its iCalUID: the vendor's migration path. Unlike gcal_create_event it sends no invitations and keeps the body's organizer. The copy is a normal event afterwards (gcal_list_events with iCalUID finds it). Returns the Event resource plus organizerEmail and guestEmails.

calendarId.description: The calendar ID to import the event onto, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

event.description: Event resource to import: the same shape, key classes and dateTime/timeZone rules as gcal_create_event, with three differences: iCalUID (or ical_uid) is required and stored as given; organizer {email, displayName?} is honoured — email is required when organizer is present and the imported copy keeps that organizer, who need not be the calendar's owner (displayName is not stored, reads show the address; organizer.self and organizer.id are read-only and ignored; organizer_email is an accepted alias that must agree with organizer.email when both are given) — instead of being ignored; and eventType must be default or absent (400 "Only events with an eventType of default may be imported."). Attendees are stored with the responseStatus they arrive with. Nobody is mailed and there is no sendUpdates. An id (or event_id) you supply must be 5-1024 base32hex characters, else 400; one another event on the calendar already holds is 409, and so is an iCalUID another one-off or recurring master on this calendar already carries (409 "The requested identifier already exists."). Checks run in the order calendar 404, permission 403, body 400, taken id 409, taken iCalUID 409. Nothing is written on any refusal.
event.title: Event

tools.name: gcal_insert_acl
tools.description: Grant a principal a role on a calendar (the real acl.insert): a user or group by email, a whole email domain, or everyone (scope type default). From this write on the grantee's effective role — what gcal_list_calendars reports as accessRole and what every read, free/busy and write gate enforces — is the highest role among the rules that match them; a user granted reader or better sees the calendar on their calendar list (a removed entry is restored). group rules are stored and listed but never match anybody: this universe has no group membership. Only the calendar's owner may change access (403 otherwise). Returns the AclRule resource.

calendarId.description: The calendar whose access control list this names, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar. A calendar that does not exist or that the acting user cannot read is 404 "Calendar not found: <calendarId>", exactly as on every read.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

rule.description: AclRule to create: {role, scope: {type, value}}; role and scope.type are required, scope.value for every type but default. role is one of none, freeBusyReader, reader, writerWithoutPrivateAccess, writer, owner; scope is {type, value} with type one of default (the public scope; value is omitted), user or group (value an email address), domain (value a domain name, stored lower-cased). The read-only fields a rule just read carries (kind, etag, id) are ignored, so a read rule can be re-sent as it came. Any other key is refused with 400 and invalid_fields naming it; a missing required key is 400 "Missing role." / "Missing scope." / "Missing scope.type." / "Missing scope.value."; a value outside the vocabulary is 400 "Invalid value for <field>: <value>". The rule id is derived from the scope ("user:<email>", "group:<email>", "domain:<domain>", "default"); a rule for the same principal — the same scope type and value, compared without regard to letter case, deleted or live — is updated to this role and answered as it now stands, and its id keeps the spelling first stored. Setting the calendar owner's own user rule to anything but owner is 403 "Cannot change the owner's access to the calendar.". Checks run in the order calendar 404, permission 403, body 400, owner 403. Nothing is written on any refusal.
rule.title: Rule

sendNotifications.description: Whether to send notifications about the calendar sharing change (default true, as on the real API): a user or group granted freeBusyReader or better is mailed by the acting user through the workspace mailbox when one exists, from this write's own transaction. default and domain grants, role none, access removal ("there are no notifications on access removal"), a write that leaves the role as it was and a write with no acting user mail nobody.
sendNotifications.title: Sendnotifications

tools.name: gcal_insert_calendar
tools.description: Create a secondary calendar. The acting user is made its data owner: they own it, gcal_list_calendars reports accessRole owner on it, and it is private to them (nobody else can see it or its events). Its id is minted by the server (c_<hex>@group.calendar.google.com) and returned as id; the response is the Calendar resource. With no acting user set the calendar is created with no data owner and is visible and writable like every calendar in that mode.

calendar.description: Calendar resource to create: {summary, description?, timeZone?}. summary is required. summary is the title, a non-blank string; description a string or null (null clears it); timeZone an IANA Time Zone Database name (e.g. Europe/Zurich), else 400 Invalid value for timeZone. The read-only fields a calendar just read carries (kind, etag, id, dataOwner, autoAcceptInvitations) are ignored, so a read calendar can be re-sent as it came. location, conferenceProperties and labelProperties are not stored by this server and are refused with 400 and invalid_fields naming them; any other key is refused with 400 and invalid_fields naming it. timeZone omitted means the zone this server stamps on the primary calendars it provisions (the configured default_time_zone, else the most common zone on file, else UTC). Nothing is written on any refusal.
calendar.title: Calendar

tools.name: gcal_insert_calendar_list_entry
tools.description: Add an existing calendar to the acting user's calendar list, or restore one removed with gcal_delete_calendar_list_entry, setting the per-user fields (colorId, hidden, selected, summaryOverride, defaultReminders, notificationSettings) the body carries. A calendar already on the list answers its entry updated with those fields. Returns the CalendarListEntry as gcal_list_calendars shows it, accessRole included. Requires an acting user (the list is theirs); with none set this is 400 Invalid Value.

entry.description: CalendarList entry to add: {id, colorId?, hidden?, selected?, summaryOverride?, defaultReminders?, notificationSettings?}. id is the calendar to add (or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar) and is required. colorId is a palette id, "1" to "24" as gcal_get_colors lists them (null clears it; backgroundColor and foregroundColor are derived from it and ignored when sent, as the real API ignores them without colorRgbFormat); hidden and selected are booleans; summaryOverride a string or null (null clears it); defaultReminders a list of {method, minutes} with method one of email, popup and minutes an integer from 0 to 40320; notificationSettings {notifications: [{type, method}]} with type one of eventCreation, eventChange, eventCancellation, eventResponse, agenda and method email, or null to clear it. The read-only fields an entry just read carries (kind, etag, summary, description, location, timeZone, accessRole, primary, deleted, dataOwner, conferenceProperties, autoAcceptInvitations, backgroundColor, foregroundColor) are ignored, so a read entry can be re-sent as it came. Any other key is refused with 400 and invalid_fields naming it. The calendar must already be readable by the acting user (owned, shared with them, or domain/anyone-visible); one that is not is 404 Calendar not found, exactly as on a read, and sharing is never changed by this tool. Checks run in the order body 400 (the calendar id is in the body, so it is read before the calendar is looked up), then calendar 404. Nothing is written on any refusal.
entry.title: Entry

tools.name: gcal_list_acl
tools.description: List the access control rules of a calendar: who holds which role on it, as {kind: "calendar#acl", etag, items: [{kind, etag, id, scope: {type, value}, role}], totalResults, nextPageToken?}. Rules are ordered by id (default, then domain:, group:, user:). Requires writer or owner on the calendar (the vendor gives writers read access to the ACLs): a reader or writerWithoutPrivateAccess is 403, a calendar the acting user cannot read is 404 Calendar not found. With no acting user every calendar is owner and every rule is listed.

calendarId.description: The calendar whose access control list this names, or "primary" for the acting user's own calendar. A calendar that does not exist or that the acting user cannot read is 404 "Calendar not found: <calendarId>", exactly as on every read.
calendarId.title: Calendarid

maxResults.description: Maximum number of rules returned on one page, 1 to 250 (default 100); 0 or less is a 400 Invalid Value naming maxResults; larger values are clamped to 250.
maxResults.title: Maxresults

pageToken.description: Token for fetching the next page, exactly as returned in nextPageToken (the literal form "offset:<n>"). Anything else, including an explicitly empty string, is refused as a 400 Invalid Value naming pageToken; omit it for the first page.
pageToken.title: Pagetoken

showDeleted.description: Whether to include deleted rules, which are kept with role none (the vendor's representation of a deleted ACL); false leaves them out.
showDeleted.title: Showdeleted

tools.name: gcal_list_calendars
tools.description: List calendars visible to the acting user. Every persona the universe knows — a calendar owner or sharee, a contacts roster persona or a gmail mailbox owner — has a primary calendar whose id is their own address, provisioned when the seed carried none, so the acting persona's own calendar is always listed and "primary" resolves to it. A persona on none of those sources is warned about when set as the acting user and sees only domain/anyone-visible calendars. The list is the acting user's: gcal_insert_calendar_list_entry / gcal_delete_calendar_list_entry change membership without changing sharing, and the per-user fields colorId, backgroundColor, foregroundColor, hidden, selected, summaryOverride, defaultReminders and notificationSettings come from their entry.

minAccessRole.description: The minimum access role the acting user must hold on a returned entry, compared by rank against accessRole: one of freeBusyReader, reader, writer, writerWithoutPrivateAccess, owner (the rank order is freeBusyReader < reader < writerWithoutPrivateAccess < writer < owner). With no acting user every entry is owner, so the filter keeps everything. Omitted means no restriction.
minAccessRole.title: Minaccessrole

maxResults.description: Maximum number of entries returned on one page, 1 to 250 (default 100); 0 or less is a 400 Invalid Value naming maxResults; larger values are clamped to 250.
maxResults.title: Maxresults

pageToken.description: Token for fetching the next page, exactly as returned in nextPageToken (the literal form "offset:<n>"). Anything else, including an explicitly empty string, is refused as a 400 Invalid Value naming pageToken; omit it for the first page.

showDeleted.description: Whether to include calendar list entries the acting user removed with gcal_delete_calendar_list_entry (returned with deleted: true); with no acting user nothing is deleted and both values return the same list.

A date-only, offset-less or empty value is refused with a 400 naming the parameter; omitted means no bound. tools.name: gdocs_batch_update
tools.description: Apply a list of update requests to a Doc (mirrors POST /v1/documents/{documentId}:batchUpdate), returning {documentId, driveFileId, modifiedTime, replies, writeControl}. `replies` has one entry per request, in order, keyed by request kind as in the Docs API Response union: `{"replaceAllText": {"occurrencesChanged": N}}` for a replaceAllText (0 is a success, and still a new revision), `{}` for insertText, deleteContentRange and the four style kinds. Failures are `{error: {code, status, message}}` and write nothing: 404 NOT_FOUND when no Doc carries the id; 403 PERMISSION_DENIED both for a Doc the acting persona may not read ("The caller does not have permission") and for one it can read but may not edit (the owner and `writer` grantees may); 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT for a malformed request. 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT also for a malformed `writeControl` or a `requiredRevisionId` that is not the document's current revision (nothing is written; read the document again).

documentId.description: The ID of the document to update.
documentId.title: Documentid

requests.description: Non-empty list of update requests to apply, in order and atomically; supported kinds are `insertText`, `replaceAllText`, `deleteContentRange`, `updateTextStyle`, `updateParagraphStyle`, `createParagraphBullets` and `deleteParagraphBullets`, each using Google's Docs API request schema; any other kind fails the whole batch with `unsupported request kind: <kind>`. Each request object carries exactly one kind. Every request is validated before anything is applied: an empty list, an empty or multi-kind request object, an `insertText` whose `text` is missing or empty, or any other invalid request fails the whole batch and nothing is written (no new revision, `modifiedTime` unchanged); an unknown or invisible document is not-found and a read-only one is permission-denied before any request is looked at. `insertText` takes exactly one of `location: {index}` or `endOfSegmentLocation: {}` (append to the end of the body); a request with neither, or with both, fails the whole batch. Indices count UTF-16 code units (an emoji occupies two) and address the body segment gdocs_get_document reports: index 1 is the first character, the last paragraph's terminating newline sits at `content[-1].endIndex - 1`, and that is the highest index an `insertText` may name (it appends after the last character); an index at or past the segment end is refused with `Index N must be less than the end index of the referenced segment, M.`, as is an index that would split a surrogate pair. A `deleteContentRange` must lie inside the segment and may not cover that terminating newline, which the body always keeps. `replaceAllText` is `{containsText: {text, matchCase?, searchByRegex?}, replaceText}`: `matchCase` and `searchByRegex` are JSON booleans (a string such as "false" is refused) and default to false, so matching is case-insensitive and literal; with `searchByRegex: true` the `text` is a regular expression (Python `regex` engine, not the vendor's RE2: lookaround and backreferences work, `\Q..\E` does not) and every match is replaced (`replaceText` is inserted literally, no group references), while an invalid pattern, or one that takes more than 2 seconds to match the document, fails the batch; `tabsCriteria` is accepted and ignored because every Doc here has a single tab. Paragraph styles and bullets follow the paragraph: inserted text joins the paragraph it lands in (a newline-terminated insert at a paragraph's first character yields new paragraphs carrying that paragraph's style), `replaceAllText` re-anchors the paragraphs after each replacement, and removing a paragraph break merges the paragraphs under the first one's style; only a paragraph emptied at the very end of the body loses its style. The four style kinds take `range: {startIndex, endIndex}` with `1 <= startIndex < endIndex <= content[-1].endIndex` (the terminating newline may be styled; `segmentId` is refused, `tabId` ignored). `updateTextStyle` needs a non-empty `fields` mask naming any of `bold`, `italic`, `underline`, `strikethrough`, `smallCaps`, `link` (or `*`): a masked property present in `textStyle` is set (booleans; `link` is `{url}`), a masked property absent from it is reset, any other TextStyle property is refused; the paragraph is then read back as several textRuns, one per span of uniform style, and text inserted later takes the style of the character before it. `updateParagraphStyle` masks `namedStyleType` only (`NORMAL_TEXT`, `TITLE`, `SUBTITLE`, `HEADING_1`..`HEADING_6`; absent in the mask resets to `NORMAL_TEXT`) on every paragraph the range overlaps. `createParagraphBullets` puts every overlapped paragraph in one list with `bulletPreset` (default `BULLET_DISC_CIRCLE_SQUARE`), joining the preceding paragraph's list when its preset matches; leading tabs set the nesting level and are removed, which shifts every later index in the batch by the tabs removed, as the vendor does. `deleteParagraphBullets` removes the bullets of the overlapped paragraphs. Each of the four replies `{}`.
requests.title: Requests

tools.name: gdocs_get_document
tools.description: Get a Google Doc (mirrors GET /v1/documents/{documentId}), returning the full Docs-API-shaped document including body.content. `body.content[0]` is the section break every body opens with (index 0 to 1); every later element is a paragraph whose textRuns concatenate to its text ending with its newline, the last paragraph included — one textRun per span of uniform character style, a single one when the paragraph carries none — so the last element's endIndex is the text length plus two and `content[-1].endIndex - 1` is the index that appends after the last character. Concatenating the text runs gives the string gdocs_get_document_text returns, except that a document with no text renders as one paragraph holding just a newline while that tool reads it as "". All startIndex/endIndex values count UTF-16 code units: an emoji or other astral character occupies two. `fields` applies Google's partial-response mask; `includeTabsContent: true` moves body, documentStyle, namedStyles and lists under a single `tabs[0].documentTab`; `suggestionsViewMode` is accepted and changes nothing here. A bulleted paragraph carries `bullet {listId, nestingLevel}` (also mirrored under `paragraphStyle`), and `lists` maps every list this server created to its glyph presets; lists ingested from a universe carry no `lists` entry. `name`, `createdTime` and `modifiedTime` are synthetic additions — the real Document resource has none; the stamps live on the Drive file. Failures are `{error: {code, status, message}}`: 404 NOT_FOUND when no Doc carries the id; 403 PERMISSION_DENIED ("The caller does not have permission") when the Doc exists but the acting persona may not read it — request access or act as a persona that has it, the id is not wrong; 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT for a malformed `fields` mask or one naming a field the Document resource does not have at that level, or an unknown `suggestionsViewMode`, named in `invalid_fields`, decided before the id is looked up.

Names at every level are the Document resource's own field names (camelCase or snake_case), plus this server's `name`, `createdTime`, `modifiedTime`; a valid name this server never populates selects nothing, and a name the Document resource does not have at that level is refused with 400 `Invalid field selection <name>`. Omitted or empty returns every field.

suggestionsViewMode.description: One of DEFAULT_FOR_CURRENT_ACCESS, SUGGESTIONS_INLINE, PREVIEW_SUGGESTIONS_ACCEPTED, PREVIEW_WITHOUT_SUGGESTIONS. Accepted and validated; no Doc here carries suggestions, so every mode returns the same content and indices. Any other value is refused with 400.

tools.name: get_time
tools.description: Returns the current date and time for this environment. The clock on the machine you are running on is not synchronized with this environment, so do not use it and do not rely on your own assumption about today's date. Call this tool and derive from its value every absolute date, time or timestamp you pass to another tool, and every relative phrase you resolve ("today", "this week", "overdue", "the last 30 days"). current_time is in UTC, as are the dates and times the other tools here take, so derive those from current_time. If you have been told your user's IANA time zone, you can pass it as time_zone to also get local_time, the same instant in that zone, for telling your user the time in their own terms; it does not change the dates you pass to tools. A date taken from any other source can silently match no records on a read, or file a record at the wrong time on a write. Time advances while you work, so re-read this before each write rather than reusing an earlier value. Inside a raw SQL or free-form query string, prefer the literal date this tool returns over CURRENT_DATE or NOW(), so the query is reproducible.
